comparator.sourceNotes: Adopted ESSB 2026–2027 EER Appendix III C, page 39, confirms all 23 credited components and 60+60+60 EC for English-language MISOC. It includes first-year Designing Social Research (6.5 EC) omitted from the university's public overview. Year 2 includes an independent 7.5-EC Research Project; year 3 includes 15-EC minor and compulsory 15-EC Bachelor Project. Open minor choice is not populated. This is guarded v2 recovery of an existing record: the earlier root production decision did not exist and is not claimed to have been replayed. questionsApplications.label: How can public organisations manage challenges that cross national borders?

alternatives.concept: Closest feasible multidisciplinary approximation of MISOC, combining public administration, politics, international law, sociology, economics, organisation and social-research methods around international social challenges.
alternatives.labelRationale: The visible label was reviewed after completion of the 24-course curriculum and accurately presents this option as the closest feasible UCR response to Bachelor in Management of International Social Challenges, rather than as a narrower subfield.

alternatives.concept: A climate and sustainability governance route that uses the programme's explicit climate-change challenge as the organising question and combines environmental systems, governance, sociology, economics, law and communication.

alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Compared with the broad closest match, this route replaces seven courses (52.5 EC) with environmental systems, sustainability governance, circular-resource study, renewable-system design, applied sustainability research and public communication. Those changes follow directly from the evidenced climate-change and Sustainable Development Goals direction.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The broad closest match and the climate/sustainability governance route are both defensible. The climate route is the strongest additional option because its evidence produces a genuine seven-course curricular shift. A migration/development candidate could not support a third alternative: the substitutions needed to cross the threshold did not implement migration or development and therefore failed qualitative distinctness. The technology-and-public-organisations interest was also assessed for completeness and found not feasible as a coherent 24-course route.

notes.text: The Erasmus programme combines a structured Public Administration curriculum with international law, migration, development, research methods and a bachelor project. UCR can assemble strong multidisciplinary programmes around global governance and specific international challenges, but does not reproduce the same dedicated MISOC sequence or its named International Migration and Global Development Issues courses.

audience.programmeDescription: Management of International Social Challenges at Erasmus University Rotterdam examines how public organisations address problems across national borders, including migration, global development, climate change and economic instability. Students study politics, policy, international law, sociology, economics and management alongside social research and a bachelor project.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The closest UCR option combines substantial governance, international law, political, social, economic, organisational and research study. A second option focuses on climate and sustainability governance, including complementary environmental science and technology. These are related UCR programmes rather than equivalents to Erasmus’s dedicated MISOC curriculum; the specialist migration and development courses, policy-analysis sequence and required 15-EC bachelor project remain gaps.
